title: Logging out does not log anybody out
summary: Log out clears the client and the credentials it cleared go on working. Make it land on the next request: refreshing replaces the refresh token and leaves the old one worth nothing, logging out ends one session without touching the others, and a refresh token that turns up twice ends the session it came from.

checkpoints.title: A login opens a session and its access token gets in
checkpoints.hint: This half arrives working, so a failure here is something the rest of the work broke. The handlers read the caller off request.auth, and a Nest guard that returns false answers 403 where these want 401.

checkpoints.title: Refreshing rotates the refresh token
checkpoints.hint: Rotation is two writes rather than one: the token you were handed stops being the live one, and a new one takes its place against the same session. The session id inside the access token does not change, because refreshing is not a second login.

checkpoints.title: Logging out takes effect on the next request
checkpoints.hint: A signature check consults nothing, so nothing you write can fail one. The guard has the session in claims.sessionId and the store has findSession; logging out everywhere is sessionsFor followed by revokeSession on each.

checkpoints.title: A refresh token that turns up twice ends the session
checkpoints.hint: Deleting the old row on rotation loses the difference between a value that was never issued and one that was spent, and both then look identical on the way in. markTokenUsed keeps that difference, and the answer to a spent one is to end the session rather than only to refuse the request.
